set.body:
Prototype and decide whether the complete SampleSpace becomes the principal static owner.

Compare
- Current Sampled[F,D,A,Role,R].
- Sampled[S,A,Sem,R] with SampleSpace[S].
- A value-singleton/path-dependent SampleSpace owner.
- Any narrowly better alternative discovered by the spike.

Prototype workloads
- Common D3 image construction with regular Time axis.
- selectTime/axis selection, crop, flip, permutation, and stride.
- Fresh derived sample-space owners.
- Independently restored spaces aligned and rebound without copying.
- SomeSampled and runtime-loaded rank/dimension.
- Same-owner zipWith as a total operation.
- Generic downstream functions that do not expose proof bookkeeping.

Acceptance criteria
- Publish a decision record with source signatures, compiler behavior, migration cost, and rejected alternatives.
- The selected owner type earns its cost by making exact same-space operations total or materially reducing repeated checks.
- Derived values retain usable captured owner types without mandatory wrapper stacks.
- Dynamic loading remains approachable.
- No runtime allocation or indirection is added to ranked data access.
- Define neutral SampleSpaceRecord and its relationship to live and persistent identity.

Tests
- Compile-only consumer fixtures for all prototype workloads.
- Negative compile-time fixtures prevent combining distinct owners without alignment.
- Alignment/rebind fixtures prove restored owners can interoperate.
- Allocation court compares ranked Sampled access before/after with direct Ravel and requires no added measured allocation.
- JVM/Scala.js API and runtime parity.
- Binary-size/optimized Scala.js inspection shows no proof-wrapper hot-path residue.
set.title: Prototype the complete sample space as the static owner
